subject: Operational guardrails & SLA amendment request — Rivermark (Private)
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@rivermark.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@rivermark.com>, procurements@rivermark.com
Date: 2028-05-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Operational guardrails & SLA amendment request — Rivermark (Private)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward onboarding Redwood Private in our EU colo, Procurement has raised a concern around the SLA language for network/egress latency and availability. Because Rivermark owns the colocation NAT, BGP peering, and the transit path from our edge to Redwood's VPC endpoint, we need a narrow exception that limits Redwood's uptime/latency commitments to the portion of the path under Redwood's operational control.

What we'd like to capture: a short appendix that states that latency and availability SLOs exclude customer-controlled WAN/peering elements, and that any outage attributable to customer-managed network configuration or third-party transit won't be counted against Redwood's SLA. Procurement has attached a suggested redline (see attached PDF).

Can we get a definitive position on whether Redwood can accept that carveout, what evidence you would require to validate incidents, and whether an operational runbook with joint escalation steps would be acceptable in lieu of changing the main SLA?

Elena
Elena Rossi
Head of Infrastructure, Rivermark Analytics
elena.rossi@rivermark.com
+44 20 7123 4567

Attachments: rivermark_sla_draft_v2.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@rivermark.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Operational guardrails & SLA amendment request — Rivermark (Private)

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the draft.

Short answer: we do support carving out customer-controlled network elements from our latency/availability SLOs for Private deployments, but we need to codify the boundary and the evidence protocol. We typically do this via a short appendix plus an attached runbook that both sides sign off on.

Before we proceed, two asks from our side:
- Can you confirm the IP prefixes and the specific peering points (colo racks / router IDs) that you consider "customer-controlled"? We need concrete identifiers for event attribution.
- For incidents you expect to attribute to Rivermark-managed transit, what telemetry (flow logs, BGP session timestamps, traceroutes) can you provide quickly during an incident? We need a minimum evidence set so our ops team can rule in/out Redwood infrastructure.

I've looped in Kimberly (security/compliance) and Priyom (account lead) to align on acceptable language and the commercial angle. Kimberly — can you advise on evidence thresholds we require (SOC/compliance-friendly)? Priyom — want to work the commercial/contracting impacts with Procurement.

I'll wait for the specifics and then propose a short appendix we can push to legal for redline.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Product Partnerships — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@rivermark.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@rivermark.com>, procurements@rivermark.com
Date: 2028-05-26T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Operational guardrails & SLA amendment request — Rivermark (Private)

Jonas — thanks for the quick reply.

Quick answers:
- Customer-controlled prefixes: 198.51.100.0/24 (edge NAT), 203.0.113.0/28 (peering VLAN), peer ASN 64512. Peering point is Equinix LD4 rack 22, router ID r-ld4-22a.
- Incident telemetry: we can share traceroute outputs, BGP session up/down timestamps, and sampled flow logs (anonymized headers). We cannot share raw packet captures for privacy reasons but can provide hashes and timing windows.

We attached a short runbook snapshot as a text file with our preferred escalation path (Rivermark NOC -> Redwood on-call -> joint incident call). Procurement is asking for: (a) explicit exclusion clause in the SLA, (b) a commitment that Redwood will not be penalized for downtime or latency when root cause is within the customer-managed network, (c) a signed runbook as a condition to onboard.

If helpful, Tom and I can do a 30-minute tech call this week to walk through the peering configs.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachments: runbook_snapshot_2028-05-26.txt
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@rivermark.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Operational guardrails & SLA amendment request — Rivermark (Private)

Elena / Tom — appreciate the detail. Happy to set up the 30-minute tech sync. I'll coordinate schedules.

From a commercial perspective, we can accept an appendix that excludes customer-controlled network elements from Redwood's latency/availability SLOs, provided:
1) The appendix lists the exact prefixes, ASNs, and colo handoff point(s) (as Elena provided).
2) The runbook contains joint escalation timelines and a defined evidence package (at minimum: BGP session logs with timestamps, traceroutes from both sides, and a short incident timeline).
3) We include a 30-day verification period post-onboarding where both sides confirm observability and exchange a short attestation.

Kimberly — can your team review the minimal evidence set and confirm it's sufficient for SOC-friendly audits? Marissa — legal will need a short redline; can you prepare a one-paragraph appendix that maps to the three items above?

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-29T16:40:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Operational guardrails & SLA amendment request — Rivermark (Private)

Kimberly / Marissa — forwarding the thread and customer attachments. Below is the draft paragraph I propose we send to Rivermark as an initial redline. If you both can sign off, I'll send it and schedule the tech sync.

--- Proposed SLA Appendix (draft) ---
"Redwood's uptime and latency commitments for Private deployments apply to the service components and network segments that are under Redwood's operational control. Customer-controlled network elements — specifically the IP prefixes, ASNs, and physical peering points documented in Appendix A — are excluded from Redwood's latency and availability SLO calculations. In the event of an incident, the parties agree to follow the jointly-signed operational runbook; attribution will be determined using the mutually-agreed evidence package (BGP session timestamps, bidirectional traceroutes, and summarized flow logs). Where root cause analysis identifies customer-managed network configuration or third-party transit as the proximate cause, such events will not be counted as Redwood SLA violations. The parties will complete a 30-day post-onboarding observability verification and exchange attestations confirming monitoring coverage."

Notes:
- We should avoid absolute language around "no penalties" — instead say "will not be counted as Redwood SLA violations" and leave remedies to contract/legal to avoid commercial exposure.
- Kimberly: please confirm the evidence items are sufficient for compliance audits or suggest additions.
- Marissa: if legal can convert the paragraph into formal redline, we can email today.

Thanks,
Jonas
